funFact: Astronauts feel like this all day — in space, blood floats up to your head too!
story: After a big mountain hike, a little explorer found a magic resting wall. Feet up, eyes soft, and all the tiredness drained away like water.
description: Scoot your bottom close to the wall and lie back. 🧘 Swing your legs up so they rest on the wall like two tall towers. Let your arms flop, breathe slow... ahhh. You're upside down AND resting!

funFact: The tallest waterfall on Earth, Angel Falls, drops water almost one kilometer down!
story: Imagine your legs are a sparkling waterfall pouring up into the sky — the only waterfall in the world that flows UP!
description: Lie on your back and float your legs straight up to the sky. 💦 Wiggle your toes like splashing water. Now let your legs be still and tall. Breathe slow and enjoy your waterfall!

funFact: Gorillas are gentle giants — they mostly munch plants all day long.
story: A curious gorilla heard footsteps behind her. Instead of turning around, she bent over and peeked between her own legs — hee hee, the world looks funny upside down!
description: Stand with your feet wide like a big strong gorilla. 🦍 Bend forward and let your head hang down. Now peek between your legs — who's behind you? Wave hello upside down!

funFact: When you hang your head down, your brain gets a whoosh of fresh, oxygen-rich blood!
story: The Upside-Down Explorer discovered a secret: if you look at the world between your knees, the floor becomes the sky and clouds become puddles!
description: Stand with your back near a wall for a cozy safe spot. 🙃 Fold forward, hang your head, and look at your upside-down world. What do you see? Ceilings are the new floors! Slowly roll up when you're done.

funFact: Sloths can hang upside down for hours — even while they sleep!
story: A sleepy sloth let go of everything — arms, head, worries — and just dangled in the warm jungle breeze, smiling slowly.
description: Stand tall, then flop forward like a super sleepy sloth. 🦥 Let your arms dangle, let your head hang heavy. Sway gently side to side... sooo relaxing. Roll up slowly, one bone at a time!

funFact: Some real bridges lift up and down to let tall boats sail through!
story: The magic bridge rises slooowly to let a sailboat pass, then rolls back down, one stone at a time, until the road is flat again.
description: Lie on your back, bend your knees, feet flat on the floor. 🌉 Press your feet down and roll your hips up, up, up — you're a lifting bridge! Now roll down slooowly, one back-bump at a time. Boat's through — lift again!

funFact: Dogs stretch like this every time they wake up from a nap — it's called a play bow!
story: A little puppy wanted to do the big-dog stretch, so she put her paws on the wall and made her very first upside-down V. Woof!
description: Stand facing the wall and press your paws flat on it. 🐶 Walk your feet back and bow forward until your body makes a big letter L. Push the wall away and stretch that puppy back — woof woof!

funFact: Bears can run faster than the fastest human — even walking on all fours!
story: Big Bear lumbered through the forest looking for berries, bottom up, head down, sniffing the ground with every giant step.
description: Put your hands and feet on the floor and push your bottom high in the air. 🐻 Now WALK, big bear! Right paw, left foot, stomp stomp. Keep your head down and growl a friendly GRRR!

benefits: Gets you ready for big inversions
funFact: Dolphins sleep with one half of their brain awake so they remember to swim up and breathe!
story: A young dolphin practiced diving nose-first through the waves, forearms like flippers, ready for the big ocean show.
description: Kneel down and put your forearms on the floor like flat flippers. 🐬 Tuck your toes, lift your hips high, and make a pointy dolphin dive shape. Press your flippers down and peek at your feet. Eee-ee-ee!

funFact: Dolphins can swim up to 60 kilometers per hour when they're excited!
story: Splash! The little dolphin tip-toed her tail closer and closer to her nose, getting ready to leap through the sparkly hoop.
description: Start in Dolphin Pose with forearms down and hips high. 🐬 Now tip-toe your feet toward your elbows — tiny steps, splash splash! Hips go higher with every step. Then walk back out and try again!

funFact: Dogs really do stand on three legs sometimes — usually to say hello to a fire hydrant!
story: Rocket the dog smelled adventure in the sky, so he lifted one leg high like a furry rocket ship counting down to blast off!
description: Make your upside-down V: hands down, hips up, head relaxed. 🐕 Now float one leg up to the sky — three-legged dog! Point your toes like a rocket. Hold it... and switch legs. Blast off!

funFact: A dog wagging its tail to the right side usually means it's extra happy!
story: When Biscuit the dog heard the word W-A-L-K, her tail wagged so hard her whole upside-down body wiggled with joy!
description: Get into your Down Dog V — hands down, tail up! 🐕 Now wag that happy tail! Wiggle your hips left and right, left and right. Someone said WALKIES! Keep those arms strong while you wag!

funFact: The very top of your head is called the crown — like where a king wears his hat!
story: A young wizard learned that pointing the crown of your head at the earth charges you up with quiet, sparkly calm.
description: Step your feet super wide like a giant triangle. 🔻 Fold forward slowly and let the top of your head sink toward the floor. Hands on the ground for balance. You're a mighty upside-down mountain — breathe!

funFact: Yogis call shoulderstand poses 'all-limb poses' because your whole body works together as a team.
story: A little firefly practiced glowing at half-brightness first — legs tilted like a cozy lantern — before shining at full beam.
description: Lie on your back and swing your legs up and over a little, lifting your hips off the floor. 🕯️ Hold your lower back with your hands like a shelf. Let your legs lean over your face like a half-lit candle. Breathe softly!
safetyNote: Keep your weight on your shoulders and arms, not your neck, and keep your head still — no looking side to side.

funFact: Resting with your legs above your heart helps your body feel fresh, like plugging in to recharge.
story: The sleepy dragon stacked soft pillows under her hips, floated her legs to the sky, and dreamed of flying without flapping once.
description: Lie back with a folded blanket or cushion under your hips. 🛏️ Float your legs up to the sky and let the cushion do the holding. Arms rest on the floor. You're upside down the comfy way!
safetyNote: Keep your head and neck relaxed on the floor and your chin pointing up — no turning your head.

funFact: Polar bears have black skin under all that white fur to soak up the warm sun!
story: The polar bear cub found her own paw prints in the snow and followed them backwards, all the way home to her cozy den.
description: Hands and feet on the floor, bottom high — bear shape! 🐻‍❄️ Now walk BACKWARDS: foot back, paw back, slow and steady. Peek under your arm to see where you're going. Careful bear steps!

funFact: A rabbit's powerful back legs can hop nearly three meters in one jump!
story: The bravest bunny in the meadow practiced her happy hops — hands planted, fluffy tail bouncing to the sky — training for the Great Carrot Games.
description: Crouch down and plant your hands flat like strong bunny paws. 🐰 Look at the floor between your hands. Now hop your feet up behind you — boing! Little hops, tail to the sky! Land soft on quiet feet.

benefits: Gets you ready for forearm stand
funFact: Dolphins leap out of the water partly just for fun — scientists think they love to play!
story: One flick of her tail and the show-dolphin lifted her flukes high above the waves while the crowd cheered, 'Eee-eee-hooray!'
description: Start in Dolphin Pose, forearms pressing down like strong flippers. 🐬 Tip-toe your feet in, then float ONE leg way up to the sky. Point your toes like a dolphin tail! Hold... then switch. Splash!
safetyNote: Practice on a soft mat with lots of space, and keep both forearms pressing down the whole time.

funFact: Your arms can hold up your whole body — they get stronger every single time you practice!
story: The clever mountain dog found a cliff wall and walked his paws right up it, making a perfect letter L that all the other dogs admired.
description: Sit with your feet touching the wall, then flip to hands and knees facing away. 🦮 Press your hands down and walk your feet UP the wall until your legs are straight out — you're a big letter L! Strong arms, happy dog!
safetyNote: Only with a grown-up spotter close by. Use a soft mat under your hands and walk down slowly when you're done.

funFact: Yogis nickname this pose 'the candle' because your body stands straight up like a tall flame.
story: When the sun went down, the little yogi became a candle — feet flickering high like a golden flame lighting up the whole room.
description: Lie on your back and roll your legs up and over. 🕯️ Hold your back with both hands like a strong shelf, then stretch your legs straight up to the sky. You're a tall glowing candle! Breathe slow and steady.
safetyNote: Only with a grown-up helping. Keep weight on your shoulders and arms — never on your neck alone — and never turn your head while up.

funFact: A plow is a farm tool that folds the soil over — just like your body folds over in this pose!
story: The friendly farmer's plow folded neatly over the field at sunset, tucking the seeds in for the night like a big earthy blanket.
description: Lie on your back and roll your legs up and alllll the way over your head. 🚜 Let your toes reach toward the floor behind you. Keep your arms pressing into the mat. You're a folding farm plow — beep beep!
safetyNote: Only with a grown-up helping, on a soft mat. Keep weight on your shoulders — never on your neck alone — and keep your head perfectly still.

funFact: A tripod has three legs — your two hands and head make three strong points, like a camera stand!
story: Inside its cozy shell, the little egg balanced perfectly on its nest of three twigs, waiting for the magical moment to hatch.
description: Crouch down and make a triangle: head gently on the mat in front, hands flat beside it. 🥚 Slooowly rest your knees on your bent elbows like little shelves. Tuck up tight — you're a balancing egg! Hold... and come down softly.
safetyNote: Only with a grown-up spotter on a soft mat. Most of your weight stays in your hands and arms — never press hard on your head or neck.

funFact: Donkeys kick their back legs up when they're feeling playful and frisky!
story: Pepito the donkey was SO excited about carrot day that he kicked his back hooves at the clouds — hee-haw, hee-HAW!
description: Hands flat on the mat, look between them. 🐴 Now kick your back hooves up behind you — hee-haw! One quick kick, land soft. Again! Let your hips fly a little higher each time, arms strong like fence posts.
safetyNote: Only with a grown-up spotter, on a soft mat with lots of clear space around you. Small kicks first!

funFact: Wheelbarrows were invented in ancient China more than 1,800 years ago!
story: The garden gnomes loaded their wheelbarrow with giggles instead of dirt, and it rolled all the way across the yard on two strong little hands.
description: Put your hands on the floor and let your helper gently hold your ankles. 🛞 Now walk on your hands — step, step, step! You're a wiggly wheelbarrow full of giggles. Tell your helper when you want to land!
safetyNote: Only with a careful grown-up holding your legs, on a soft surface. Stop and rest the moment your arms feel tired.

funFact: Flamingos can balance on one leg even while they're fast asleep!
story: The fanciest flamingo in the lagoon took a bow so deep that one pink leg lifted all the way to the sky — ta-daaa!
description: Stand tall, then fold forward and put your fingertips on the floor. 🦩 Now float one leg up behind you, higher and higher! Head hangs down, leg reaches for the clouds. Wobbling is part of the fun — switch sides!
safetyNote: Practice near a wall for balance, with a grown-up nearby and space around you.

funFact: With your knees hugging your ears, the whole world goes whisper-quiet — like your own secret sound-proof room!
story: The little snail curled all the way into her shell, knees to ears, and listened to the softest, quietest quiet she had ever heard.
description: From Plow Pose, bend your knees sloooowly down beside your ears. 🐌 Let your knees give your ears a gentle hug — shhh, everything goes quiet! Curl up like a cozy snail and take soft breaths.
safetyNote: Advanced pose — only with a grown-up spotter on a soft mat. Weight stays on shoulders, never on your neck alone, and keep your head totally still.

funFact: Yogis call headstand the 'king of poses' — kings and queens both love wearing their crowns upside down!
story: High in the mountain temple, the young yogi finally balanced like a still, upside-down mountain — and felt like royalty of the whole sky.
description: Clasp your hands, put your forearms down, and cradle the back of your head. 👑 Tuck your toes, walk your feet in, and let a grown-up help float your legs up. Press your forearms down hard — they carry you, like a royal throne!
safetyNote: Advanced — ONLY with a grown-up spotter, on a soft mat, near a wall. Your forearms carry the weight, never your neck alone. Skip it if your head or neck hurts.

funFact: Photographers use tripods because three points of contact make the steadiest stand!
story: Click! The upside-down photographer turned herself into a human tripod, so steady that not one picture came out blurry.
description: Make your triangle: head gently down in front, hands flat beside it like camera legs. 📷 With your grown-up helping, lift your legs straight up from Tripod Egg. Push the floor away with strong hands. Steady... say cheese!
safetyNote: Advanced — ONLY with a grown-up spotter on a soft mat. Hands and arms carry most of the weight, never your neck alone. Come down at the first wobble you can't fix.

funFact: Moving one leg at a time upside down teaches your brain amazing body maps!
story: The upside-down acrobat opened her legs like giant scissors, snip-snip, cutting ribbons of cloud in the circus sky.
description: From your steady headstand with a grown-up close, slooowly lower one leg toward the floor while the other reaches up. ✂️ Open like careful scissors... then float back together and switch. Slow is strong!
safetyNote: Advanced — ONLY with a grown-up spotter on a soft mat, after headstand feels steady. Forearms carry the weight, never your neck alone.

funFact: This pose is named for a peacock lifting its dazzling tail feathers to the sky!
story: The proud peacock swept his shimmering tail feathers straight up to the sun, and the whole garden gasped at the upside-down rainbow.
description: Start in Dolphin Pose, forearms pressed down strong. 🦚 With your grown-up spotting you, kick your legs up like glorious peacock feathers! Squeeze your legs together, point your toes, and shine!
safetyNote: Advanced — ONLY with a grown-up spotter, on a soft mat near a wall. Keep forearms pressing down; come down softly the moment you tire.

funFact: Even circus performers practice against walls first — every expert starts with a helper!
story: The young peacock practiced his grand feather-lift beside the garden wall, letting it catch his heels until his balance grew show-ready.
description: Set up Dolphin Pose with your fingertips near the wall. 🦚 With your grown-up helping, kick your heels up to rest gently on the wall. Press those forearms down! The wall is your friendly catcher — breathe and balance.
safetyNote: Advanced — ONLY with a grown-up spotter and a soft mat. Kick up gently so your heels land softly, and come down slowly one leg at a time.

funFact: The Sanskrit name means 'upside-down tree' — your hands are the roots and your feet are the branches!
story: In the topsy-turvy forest, one brave tree decided to grow the other way — roots to the sky, branches in the earth — and it became the most famous tree of all.
description: Plant your hands like strong roots, shoulder-width apart. 🤸 With your grown-up spotting, kick up one leg, then the other, and grow tall like an upside-down tree! Squeeze everything tight and look at your root-hands.
safetyNote: Advanced — ONLY with a grown-up spotter, on a soft mat with clear space. Learn to safely step or cartwheel out before holding it.

funFact: Gymnasts spend years practicing wall handstands — the wall is the world's most patient teacher!
story: Every morning, the little climber high-fived the wall and flipped upside down beside it, and every morning she balanced one blink longer.
description: Put your hands on the mat a small step from the wall. 🧗 With your grown-up helping, kick your heels up to rest on the wall. Push the floor away, strong arms! The wall's got your back — breathe and count your balance blinks!
safetyNote: Advanced — ONLY with a grown-up spotter and a soft mat. Kick up gently and come down one leg at a time, slow and controlled.

funFact: A scorpion curls its tail up over its back — and glows under ultraviolet light!
story: The desert scorpion curled her tail over her head like a glowing question mark, asking the moon, 'How high can I bend tonight?'
description: Start in your wall forearm stand with your grown-up spotting. 🦂 Slooowly bend your knees and let your toes creep down the wall toward your head — a curling scorpion tail! Tiny moves only. Then straighten up and float down.
safetyNote: Very advanced — ONLY for experienced kids with a grown-up spotter, soft mat, and wall. Tiny bends only; stop right away if your back or neck feels pinchy.

funFact: Butterflies taste with their feet — imagine tasting the sky upside down!
story: An upside-down butterfly folded her wings into a diamond and hovered perfectly still, sipping sunshine from the clouds below her feet.
description: From your steady headstand with your grown-up close, press the soles of your feet together and let your knees open wide. 🦋 Your legs make butterfly wings in the sky! Flutter gently... then float your legs back up.
safetyNote: Advanced — ONLY with a grown-up spotter on a soft mat, after headstand feels easy and steady. Forearms carry the weight, never your neck alone.
